Subject: Pilot terms - early termination / ramp protections

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week — the team is excited to run the 90-day pilot for checkout fraud detection. Before we lock dates, procurement raised two asks that are blocking signature: a) an early-termination opt-out if the pilot materially underperforms, and b) a defined ramp schedule with downsell protections so we can de-risk spend during the pilot ramp.

Specifically:
- Early termination: We need a 30-day opt-out within the first 45 days if SLA/quality targets are not met, with a capped termination fee (not to exceed 20% of committed pilot spend).
- Ramp schedule: We want a 6-week ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100% usage milestones) and an automatic downsell protection that reduces committed capacity and price if we fail to hit milestone 2.

Can Redwood provide language for an addendum — or confirm a similar commercial approach? Procurement would like this in a single-sheet addendum so their legal team can run it through.

I've attached a mutual action plan with dates.

Thanks,
Alex

Marissa / team —

Reviewed the proposed Option A. Legal is comfortable with the commercial structure provided we add two guardrails and tweak language:

1) Add a minimum-run protection: If customer reduces committed capacity below 30% of initial committed baseline at any point, Redwood reserves the right to terminate the pilot with 14 days notice and invoice for unrecoverable provisioning costs (capped at the termination fee). This prevents pathological downsizing.

2) Clarify SLA measurement and evidence: SLA misses must be documented in our usage and quality dashboards and shared in a weekly report; fee waiver only applies if the documented shortfall is material (>10%) for two consecutive reporting weeks and Redwood has not reasonably remediated after a 7-day cure period.

Proposed clean clause language (for the addendum):
"Early Termination & Ramp Adjustments: Customer may terminate the Pilot within the first forty-five (45) days upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Redwood. In the event of such termination, Customer will pay an early termination fee equal to fifteen percent (15%) of the remaining unpaid Pilot commitment, unless termination is the result of a documented and material failure by Redwood to meet Service Levels (as defined below), in which case the early termination fee will be waived. Ramp milestones and automatic capacity adjustments shall be implemented as set forth in the Mutual Action Plan; however, Customer may not reduce committed capacity below thirty percent (30%) of the initial committed baseline. If Customer does so, Redwood may terminate the Pilot upon fourteen (14) days' notice and invoice for unrecoverable provisioning costs (not to exceed the early termination fee)."

I also recommend we include a one-paragraph bullet in the addendum that lists SLA metrics used for the waiver (precision, recall, latency) and points to the MAP dashboard URL. Vivek — please confirm the provisioning cost cap looks reasonable operationally.

If everyone is good, I’ll redline the docx and return a clean addendum for signature.

- Laura
